stops.note: a plain word for a bow or arch
named an arch, especially of a bridge
Parisian shopping arcades of the early 1800s gave the word its commercial sense; video-game arcades followed in the 1970s
entered for an arched passage, later a shop-lined walkway, and eventually a venue for coin-operated games
stops.meaning: a covered, arched passageway; a games venue

current_meaning: a covered passageway with arches, or a venue for coin-operated games
